label: canon-c20-in12-eager-tb
_why: THE TIE-BREAKER of canon_c20_in12_eager_n2.json: the third run of the 2+1 rule, run ONLY if alignment_check.mjs reads the pair DIVERGENT (exit 2); the config is read as the median of three (pool both sessions in --arm). Same book, same predictions: THE BRANCH BOOK of the under-side series: building_cost = anchor x 2.0^era (600 / 1,200 / 2,400 / 4,800; 800 / 1,600 / 3,200 / 6,400) with the eager-spending define set (MONEY_SPENDING_CONSTRUCTION_TOO_LARGE_INVESTMENT_POOL_FACTOR 1.0, CRITICAL 1.25, EXCESSIVE 3.0, CONSTRUCTION_MAX_NUM_PRODUCTION_BUILDING_CONSTRUCTIONS_SCALED 0.05; LONG / VERY_LONG 160 / 240) - launched ONLY if canon-c19-in12-eager AND canon-c195-in12-eager both overshoot the band (a run above 1.3x at 1936 under the stop rule, or medians above 1.1x). It sits between C 1.95 and C 2.05 (F121: bistable - two stalls locked in by early British disasters, one growth seed at 1.32x), so the bistability risk is real and the config is not read before n=3 (the 2+1 rule's third run is expected, not exceptional). Everything but the slope as canon-c195-in12-eager.

_predictions.gdp: world GDP 0.80-1.15x at 1935 (point ~0.95); the 1900 dip 0.65-0.85x; a stall in any seed (below 0.6x after a British disaster) is F121's mechanism - the frontier too dear to rebuild - and two stalls in three end the under-side series on the cost axis.

_predictions.hoard: world pools 0.25-0.60 of GDP at 1935; the private backlog 1.0-1.5 y and the government backlog 0.9-1.6 y in every seed (the eager set's measured effect, F121); construction sector 2,800-3,800 levels
_predictions.obsolescence: rung 0 45-58% staffed at 1935 (dearer frontier, more of the old rung kept); its level count +5 to +20% from 1900; below-best 30-40%
_predictions.perf: row P total within +10% of the vanilla median play time (the found slope 0.97x); no crash expected, the deterministic resume feeder handles a mid-autosave CTD (L32)

_alignment: THE 2+1 RULE (user-ruled 2026-09-14, F114): after run 2, `node tools/testbed/ledger/alignment_check.mjs --arm <session>:canon-c20-in12-eager` - two criteria at 1935 vs the vanilla per-run median, five bands each, a pair fails an axis only in different bands AND >= 0.15 (GDP) / >= 0.10 (workers) apart. DIVERGENT => one more run of this config as its own one-run schedule (the _tb.json beside this one), the reading the median of three (pool both sessions: --arm sessA,sessB:canon-c20-in12-eager). No obsolescence criterion; rung-0 staffing / payback / below-best are verdict flags. PLUS THE RUN-LEVEL STOP (user-ruled 2026-09-14, 2+1 batches only): any run that ends above x1.3 of vanilla's 1936 GDP (the eighteen-run median at the 1936.1.1 endpoint, GBP 4,544M) is the config's LAST run - be it run 1, 2 or 3 - enforced between runs by tools/testbed/stop_watch.ps1 (drops tools/testbed/STOP after the offending run's 1936 summary lands; the next run is an 1836 stub, L17-excluded). Never mid-run. PLUS THE CAPITAL-ABUNDANCE FLAG (user-ruled 2026-09-15): `node tools/testbed/ledger/capital_flags.mjs --arm <session[,session]>:canon-c20-in12-eager` - a shortlist member (GBR, USA, FRA, GER) under 3% total unemployment INCLUDING peasants with a hoard over 2 GDP trips it; the pooled shortlist tripping is a VOID (exit 4).
